handback.title: A settings file picks each role's agent and model
handback.summary: One settings file per repo says which subscription and model the planner, worker and reviewer use; Kimi first, then Codex.
handback.feature: Each role runs on the subscription and model the owner declares in one file. Stories: setup, the file with one agent interface, Kimi, Codex.

stories.title: Setup gathers and stores a subscription's inputs
stories.user_story: The owner adds a subscription by giving its inputs once; setup puts each where runs find it.
stories.context: All of this story lives in a new `dokima/setup.py`, a command the owner runs once per subscription on their own machine. The owner did it by hand once for Kimi (comment of 2026-10-15): Kimi Code CLI 2.2.0 installed, `kimi login --region global` approved by a browser device code, then one unattended `kimi -p ... --output-format stream-json` run. Plan: Max, model access K3, default model kimi-for-coding. Agent runs start on a fresh `ubuntu-24.04` machine (`.github/workflows/agent.yml` line 49), so nothing saved on the owner's machine reaches them except through a repo secret. Hence: a key goes into a repo secret; a sign-in is done once by the agent's own login on the owner's machine (with the region the owner gives), and the files that login saves are stored as a repo secret too; the run writes them back before the agent starts (stories 3 and 4). `dokima/setup.py` holds, per agent, where its login saves the sign-in, so the adapters read the same place. Setup writes the subscription and the model into `.dokima/agents.yml` in the shape story 2 fixes: `subscriptions: <name>: {agent, key}` and `roles: <role>: {subscription, model}`, where key names the repo secret, never the secret itself. Secrets are set with `gh secret set`; tests fake `gh` with a stub on PATH and the login with a stub command.

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup lists each input a subscription needs: membership, region, sign-in or key, and model.
acceptance_criteria.words: grabbing the inputs a user needs for a subscription (membership, region, sign-in or key, model)

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup stores a key the owner gives as a repo secret, named in the settings file.
Setup signs the agent in with the owner's region and stores the saved sign-in as a repo secret.
Setup writes the subscription and the model the owner gives into the repo's settings file.

stories.title: One settings file and one agent interface
stories.user_story: Each role runs on the subscription and model the owner declares in one file; Claude Code works as today.
stories.context: Today `.github/workflows/agent.yml` fixes `MODEL: claude-opus-5-5` (line 59), installs Claude Code (line 253), runs `claude -p ... --model "$MODEL"` (line 321) and fails a run whose logs name another model (line 565). `dokima/agent_records.py` `models_used`, `run_report` and `transcript` read Claude's logs and `claude.json`; `dokima/agent_roles.py` calls them. New: `dokima/settings.py` reads `.dokima/agents.yml` (no dependencies may be added and PyYAML is absent, so a small reader of its own; `tests/test_start.py` `load_yaml` shows a subset reader). `dokima/agents.py` is the one interface: given the role, it installs, starts and reads the agent the role's subscription names, by loading the adapter module `dokima/agent_<agent>.py`, so a new agent needs only its own module. Claude Code moves into `dokima/agent_claude.py` with today's command, flags, record and stats. The workflow reads the role's key secret by name (`secrets[...]`), so new agents need no workflow change; the owner allowed the workflow change (answer 2). The owner's newest words: no fallback, and the file only declares which model each stage uses; no rules across subscriptions.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each repo keeps its agent settings in one YAML file in its Dokima folder.
The file lists subscriptions, each naming its agent and the secret holding its key.
The file gives the planner, the worker and the reviewer each a subscription and a model.
acceptance_criteria.words: `roles` (planner, worker, reviewer: which subscription and model)

acceptance_criteria.text: A role may name any model its agent takes; Dokima keeps no list of allowed models.
acceptance_criteria.words: Any agent, any model: planner, worker and reviewer each pick theirs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each run starts the agent of its role's subscription, with the model the file names.
acceptance_criteria.words: The file is just a simple declaration: which model is used for which stage.

acceptance_criteria.text: With no settings file, every run starts Claude Code with today's model, as now.
A role the file leaves out starts Claude Code with today's model, as now.
A role naming an unknown subscription or agent stops before any agent starts, and the run names the bad name.
Claude Code runs behind the one agent interface with the same command, record and stats as today.
acceptance_criteria.words: The file and one agent interface; Claude Code moves behind it unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: A model always runs in its own vendor's agent, never inside another vendor's agent.
acceptance_criteria.words: No model runs inside another vendor's agent.

acceptance_criteria.text: Moving a role to another subscription takes one edit: that role's lines in the file.
acceptance_criteria.words: It exposes a simple interface for deciding the orchestration across subscriptions.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a role's agent fails, the run fails; no other subscription takes over.

non_functional.text: Subscriptions and roles sit in their own sections, so other settings can join the file later.
non_functional.why: The owner expects the file to hold other settings later.
non_functional.words: Later it may expand into other settings.

stories.title: A role can run on Kimi Code CLI
stories.user_story: The owner moves any role to Kimi by naming a Kimi subscription for it, and spends Kimi's credit.
stories.context: Built first of the new agents, as the owner ordered (answer 1: build Kimi first, to use up its credit). All of it lives in a new `dokima/agent_kimi.py`, loaded by story 2's interface. The owner's tested command: `kimi -p ... --output-format stream-json`, Kimi Code CLI 2.2.0, model kimi-for-coding. The adapter installs Kimi's command line, writes the saved sign-in from its repo secret back where Kimi's login keeps it (the place `dokima/setup.py` names, story 1) or passes the key, and reads Kimi's stream so the record names the model used and the run's stats still show.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role on a Kimi subscription runs in Kimi Code CLI, with the Kimi model the file names.
A Kimi run writes the stored sign-in back before Kimi starts, so no one signs in again.

stories.title: A role can run on Codex CLI
stories.user_story: The owner moves any role to Codex by naming a Codex subscription for it.
stories.context: Built after Kimi, as the owner ordered ('Kimi first ... then Codex'). All of it lives in a new `dokima/agent_codex.py`, loaded by story 2's interface, following story 3's pattern: install Codex's command line, write back its stored sign-in or pass its key, read its output for the model used and the stats. Open issue 39 stays the general rule for adapters (answer 3).

acceptance_criteria.text: A role on a Codex subscription runs in Codex CLI, with the Codex model the file names.

answers.why: Story two now has one criterion for a left-out role and one for an unknown name.
